sources.name: GOV.UK Biodiversity net gain planning guidance
sources.fact: Statutory BNG generally requires at least 10% gain and a Biodiversity Gain Plan before commencement where applicable

sources.name: Understanding biodiversity net gain
sources.fact: Guidance updated 14 July 2026; BNG uses statutory biodiversity units and significant gains require long-term management

sources.name: Make on-site biodiversity gains
sources.fact: Developers can deliver 10% BNG on-site or combine with off-site mechanisms subject to the hierarchy

sources.name: What can count towards BNG
sources.fact: Different mitigation schemes count in full, in part or not at all; double counting is constrained

sources.name: BNG guidance for LPAs
sources.fact: LPAs must check biodiversity information and determine Biodiversity Gain Plans where the statutory condition applies

sources.name: Register a biodiversity gain site
sources.fact: Off-site gain sites require registration and supporting metric/legal-management evidence

sources.name: Search biodiversity gain sites register
sources.fact: Register provides site boundary, habitat and allocation information after accepted registration

sources.name: Record off-site gain allocation
sources.fact: Off-site biodiversity gains must be formally allocated to a development rather than inferred from nearby habitat

sources.name: Statutory biodiversity metric
sources.fact: The statutory metric is the official method for calculating biodiversity units

sources.name: BNG for NSIPs
sources.fact: BNG becomes mandatory for qualifying NSIP applications from 2 November 2026

sources.name: London Local Nature Recovery Strategy
sources.fact: London LNRS is a strategic spatial nature recovery tool; its map does not itself create new protections or landowner obligations

sources.name: GLA Biodiversity and BNG
sources.fact: GLA states 10% BNG applies under the statutory framework and boroughs generally implement and monitor requirements

examples: 10% statutory objective is not a parcel score without a completed metric
Nearby registered gain site does not prove units are allocated to a candidate development
LNRS potential-measure location is strategic context, not a planning designation
BNG condition is post-permission in the statutory framework and does not itself prove development viability
Habitat condition and distinctiveness require ecological survey/metric evidence, not map proximity
NSIP BNG commencement date must not be back-applied to earlier applications
Small-development exemptions changing from 6 August 2026 require application-date and scheme-specific checks
